title: Access-to-Award: Company-wide Playbook for Access, Change, Procurement and Vendor Workflows
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook, "Access-to-Award", defines the end-to-end company policies and prescriptive procedures for: access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel approvals, and the set of canonical internal templates. It is intended for all employees, hiring managers, procurement requesters, and approvers.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood employees, contractors with corporate accounts, and any supplier integrations that interact with Redwood infrastructure or corporate data.

Objectives

- Reduce time-to-approve for common procurements to <= 5 business days for requests under $10k.
- Centralize access requests with auditable approvals and 90-day revalidation cycles.
- Ensure vendor onboarding includes a standardized risk assessment and an assigned contract owner.
- Minimize unapproved configuration changes by enforcing change windows and pre-deployment checklists.

Key Roles and Responsibilities

- Requester: Submits the procurement or access request and provides business justification.
- Approver: Team manager or cost center owner who validates business need.
- Procurement Owner (Finance): Reviews supplier terms, price reasonableness, and tax/compliance checks.
- Security Reviewer: Assesses data access, required controls, and required legal addenda.
- IT/Cloud Ops: Implements access and provisioning tasks.
- Contract Owner: Maintains the vendor contract and renewal calendar.

Section 1 — Access and Permissions (Access-to-Award phase A)

Policy statements:
- Principle of least privilege enforced by default. Access is granted for a defined purpose and expiry.
- All privileges that allow data egress, escalation, or production writes require a business justification and Security approval.

Process (Steps):
1) Requester files an Access Request via the Access Portal (access.redwood.internal). Include duration, scope, and justification.
2) Manager approves or rejects within 3 business days.
3) Security performs risk review for sensitive scopes (PII, Billing, Secrets).
4) IT provisions access with a time-limited role and records audit entry.
5) Revalidation reminder triggered at 60 days, mandatory reapproval at 90 days.

Access tiers and examples:
- Tier 0: Public docs; no request required.
- Tier 1: Internal non-sensitive services (read-only dashboards). Manager approval.
- Tier 2: Sensitive systems (billing, PII). Manager + Security approval.
- Tier 3: Privileged operations (deploy write access, infra admin). Manager + Security + SRE approval.

Section 2 — Change Management

Change types:
- Routine: Configuration changes that are reversible, low risk. No CAB required if change < 15 min impact and tested in staging.
- Scheduled: Feature releases, infra scaling with >15 min expected impact — requires standard CAB review.
- Emergency: Outage mitigation — documented post-facto to CAB within 24 hours.

Change windows and SLA:
- Normal change window: Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 UTC for non-critical services. Night/weekend windows are reserved for scheduled infra changes with pre-approved rollback plans.
- Rollback capability must be demonstrable in <= 30 minutes for any change classified as Scheduled.

Pre-deployment checklist (required):
- Link to runbook and test results.
- Smoke test plan and rollback steps.
- Impacted services and owners listed.
- Performance and observability queries included.

Section 3 — Data Management

Data classification categories: PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTED. All datasets must be labeled in the data catalog.

Handling rules (high level):
- RESTRICTED: Encryption at rest + in transit, limited to named principals, storage audited monthly.
- CONFIDENTIAL: MFA enforced for access, export controls applied.

Data retention & deletion:
- Default retention for logs: 90 days (hot), 2 years (cold).
- Sensitive PII: retention only as long as required by the business process; data owner must document retention justification.

Data sharing with vendors:
- Data sharing requires: Data Processing Agreement (DPA), approved SOC/ISO evidence, and a Data Access Justification form. No PII is shared without encryption and contractual protections.

Section 4 — Procurement and Expense Approval (Access-to-Award phase B)

Purchase thresholds and path: 
| Amount range | Required approvals | Procurement path | Typical SLA |
|--------------|--------------------|------------------|-----------|
| <$1,000      | Manager            | Self-serve expense | 3 business days |
| $1,000–$25,000 | Manager + Finance  | Procurement ticket | 5–7 business days |
| >$25,000     | Manager + Finance + VP | Procurement + Contract review | 10–20 business days |

Request process (summary):
1) Create a Purchase Request in the Procurement Portal with line-item estimates and vendor info.
2) Finance validates budgets and tax implications.
3) Procurement negotiates terms and issues PO.
4) Contract Owner finalizes legal terms for >$25k or if data will be accessed by vendor.

Expense policy highlights:
- Travel expenses require pre-approval for airfare > $1,000 or international travel.
- Per diem caps and class of travel are defined in the Travel section template.

Section 5 — Vendor Management and Onboarding

Vendor risk assessment: score vendors on Security (30%), Financial stability (20%), Strategic dependency (20%), Legal/Compliance (30%). A vendor with a calculated score > 75 requires an executive sponsor and quarterly reviews.

Onboarding checklist (must be completed before production access):
- Signed contract and DPA.
- Completed vendor security questionnaire and evidence (SOC2/ISO/etc).
- Assigned Contract Owner and renewal date entered into vendor ledger.
- Technical contact, escalation path, and SLOs documented.

Sample vendor scorecard (CSV-friendly):
vendor_name,security_score,financial_score,dependency_score,legal_score,total_score,contract_owner,renewal_date
AcmeAI,85,70,60,90,76,FinOps Team,2029-05-12

Section 6 — Travel Policy (summary and pre-approval workflow)

- Business travel requires a Travel Request form with justification, estimated cost, and itinerary.
- Manager must approve domestic travel; VP approval required for international travel or events with budget > $5,000.
- Preferred booking channels: corporate travel portal; exceptions require Finance approval.

Section 7 — Templates and Forms (Appendix)

Included templates (canonical):
- Access Request Form (fields: resource, scope, duration, justification, manager)
- Procurement Request (vendor, line items, cost center, budget code, business case)
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist (contract steps, evidence required)
- Change Request Template (description, rollback plan, test plan, owners)
- Travel Request Template (dates, justification, estimated cost)

Example: Procurement request YAML snippet
---
requester: aisha.patel@redwood.com
vendor: AcmeAI
items:
  - sku: ACME-ENT-1
    description: Enterprise model endpoint (12 months)
    unit_cost: 8500
    quantity: 1
cost_center: ENG-PLATFORM
justification: Production inference capacity for Redwood Dedicated testing
---

Escalation matrix (quick):
- Day 0–3: Manager approval queue (auto-reminder).
- Day 4–7: Procurement owner escalates to Finance Lead.
- Day 8+: VP review required for unresolved high-priority requests.

Audit and Compliance

- Monthly reports: open access grants, expiring vendor contracts, pending procurements > $10k.
- Quarterly audits: random sample of access revalidation, procurement approvals, and vendor evidence.

Operational Metrics (tracked):
- Median time to approve access requests.
- % of scheduled changes with successful rollback tests.
- Time from procurement request to PO issuance.
- Vendor risk score distribution.

Change history and governance

This playbook is maintained by Finance-Legal with Security and IT as primary reviewers. Major revisions follow a documented change request and will be ratified by the Governance Board.

Contact and escalation

- Procurement Queue: procurement@redwood.internal
- Security Review: security-review@redwood.internal
- Finance Owner: finops@redwood.internal
